title: Silly season 2027: Will World of Outlaws drivers move to High Limit?
text: Brady Bacon is locked into the Vermeer 55 for 2027, and the bigger question is whether any World of Outlaws drivers follow him to High Limit. Silly season is starting, and the question people in the pits are asking is simple: will any World of Outlaws drivers make the move to…
body: Brady Bacon is locked into the Vermeer 55 for 2027, and the bigger question is whether any World of Outlaws drivers follow him to High Limit. Silly season is starting, and the question people in the pits are asking is simple: will any World of Outlaws drivers make the move to High Limit in 2027? Rumors are circulating about major changes ahead. So far, very little is confirmed. Tanner Holmes and Justin Peck are confirmed to return to High Limit in 2027. So is the Vermeer 55 team, with crew chief Tye Wolfgang back on the box. All of it was announced at the High Limit banquet the weekend of October 17 and 18. Update, October 29: The Vermeer 55 seat is filled. On October 22, team owner Tony Vermeer named Brady Bacon the full-time driver of the No. 55 for the 2027 High Limit season, with Tye Wolfgang staying on as crew chief. Bacon drove the car for the final 10 races of 2026, including a podium at Lakeside Speedway and a top five at Eldora Speedway. The four-time USAC National Sprint Car champion has 64 USAC national sprint car wins, second all-time. 2027 will be his first full-time season in a winged 410 sprint car, though he ran the winged 360 ASCS National Tour full-time from 2010 to 2012 and won 12 races. He is eligible for High Limit Rookie of the Year. The questions to follow over the winter: Does a World of Outlaws regular make the jump to High Limit? Do other teams reshuffle once the first announcements land? Until teams and series confirm their plans, treat everything beyond the names above as rumor. We will update this page as announcements come in.

title: Rico Abreu Wins Thursday World Finals Feature at Charlotte
text: Rico Abreu started third and won Thursday’s 25-lap NOS Energy Drink feature at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Tyler Courtney finished second and Bill Balog third. Rico Abreu followed his qualifying sweep with a feature win…
body: Rico Abreu started third and won Thursday’s 25-lap NOS Energy Drink feature at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Tyler Courtney finished second and Bill Balog third. Rico Abreu followed his qualifying sweep with a feature win Thursday at Charlotte. Abreu, in the Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing No. 14, started third in the 25-lap World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series main and finished ahead of Tyler Courtney and Bill Balog. Michael “Buddy” Kofoid ran fourth from sixth and Garet Williamson finished fifth after starting on the pole. David Gravel was sixth from fifth. Abreu set the night up earlier in the program. He won the WIX Filters heat from the front row and finished third in the six-lap Toyota Dash, which Williamson won over Balog. Courtney started fourth in the feature after finishing fourth in the dash. The other heat winners were Gravel, Balog and Kofoid. Logan Schuchart, Giovanni Scelzi, Logan Rumsey (from 16th) and Spencer Bayston (from 15th) completed the top 10. Parker Price-Miller won the Last Chance Showdown and Emerson Axsom won the C-main. Conner Morrell, Buddy Schweibinz, Sheldon Haudenschild and Skylar Gee were listed as DNFs. Abreu came to Charlotte off the 2026 High Limit Racing championship. On Wednesday’s qualifying night he set overall Simpson Quick Time for both Thursday (12.584) and Friday (12.542) heat lineups. Gravel came into the week going for a third straight World of Outlaws title with Big Game Motorsports. Feature points from Thursday and Friday will set heat races for Saturday’s $25,000-to-win season finale. Balog led 21 of the 25 laps on the cushion before Abreu got a run off the bottom of Turn 2 with fewer than five laps left and drove by for the lead, according to World of Outlaws. Abreu led the final four laps and won by 1.136 seconds over Courtney, earning $15,000. World of Outlaws said the win was Abreu’s 11th sprint car victory of 2026 and his second at Charlotte, and the 332nd World of Outlaws win for Tony Stewart’s operation, 14 of them at the Concord track. The World Finals continue Friday with another $15,000-to-win sprint car program.

title: Spencer Bayston Returning to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing for 2027 World of Outlaws Season
text: Bayston confirmed during the World Finals that he will drive the NOS Energy Drink No. 17 again in 2027. He and crew chief Kyle Pruitt are looking to improve after what he called “a rebuilding year.” Spencer Bayston will return to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing’s NOS Energy Drink…
body: Bayston confirmed during the World Finals that he will drive the NOS Energy Drink No. 17 again in 2027. He and crew chief Kyle Pruitt are looking to improve after what he called “a rebuilding year.” Spencer Bayston will return to Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing’s NOS Energy Drink No. 17 for the 2027 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season. Bayston confirmed the plan to Jacob Seelman of SWN on Friday, Nov. 6, during the World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. According to Seelman, Bayston said he and crew chief Kyle Pruitt have a lot they want to improve on to get the team past what he called “a rebuilding year.” The 2026 season was Bayston’s first with the team owned by Ricky Stenhouse Jr. and Richard and Jennifer Marshall, which hired him to replace Sheldon Haudenschild with Pruitt, formerly of Shark Racing, as crew chief. The pairing won the season opener on Feb. 4 at Volusia Speedway Park, where Bayston started 10th and passed Anthony Macri for the lead on lap 16. World of Outlaws statistics credit Bayston with one win, 15 top-five finishes and 36 top-10s in 68 feature starts in 2026. He finished 10th, 22nd and 12th in the three World Finals features. Bayston, of Lebanon, Ind., was the 2022 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year with CJB Motorsports and has six career World of Outlaws wins. Sunday night at the World of Outlaws Awards Celebration in Charlotte, SJMR crew member Ace Pruitt, Kyle Pruitt’s son, was named the series’ Jason Johnson Sportsman of the Year . The 2027 World of Outlaws season begins Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park’s Federated Auto Parts DIRTcar Nationals.

title: Broedy Graham Wins 2026 USAC Western States Midget Championship
text: Graham finished fourth in the Ventura finale and won his first series title by 31 points after Drake Cardey spun with two laps left. He also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup. Broedy Graham of Bakersfield, California, is the 2026 USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Western States Midget…
body: Graham finished fourth in the Ventura finale and won his first series title by 31 points after Drake Cardey spun with two laps left. He also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup. Broedy Graham of Bakersfield, California, is the 2026 USAC Avanti Windows & Doors Western States Midget champion. The 18-year-old clinched the title with a fourth-place finish in the Nov. 7 season finale at Ventura Raceway, and his BGR Racing No. 66 team won the entrant title. Graham was running sixth with two laps to go while points leader Drake Cardey ran second. Cardey was caught in a four-car tangle at the bottom of Turn 2 and spun to a stop in the infield. He finished 15th, and Graham won the championship 863-832. Graham had taken the points lead from Cardey with one race left and held a six-point edge through an eight-week break before the finale. Graham led the series with 10 top-five finishes, four fast qualifying times and five heat race wins in 12 starts, and he tied Cardey for the most top-10 finishes with 11. His first two series wins came in back-to-back weeks, in June at Merced Speedway and on July 4 at Santa Maria Speedway. He is the third Bakersfield driver in four seasons to win the title, after Brody Fuson in 2023 and Cade Lewis in 2024. Graham also won the Billy’s Tequila Cup, a points title for the three Western States Midget races at Ventura, by one point over Jett Yantis. Cardey, who won at Imperial Valley in March and Santa Maria in June for Tom Dunkel Racing, was named Rookie of the Year. Yantis led the series with five wins, and C.J. Sarna was named Most Improved Driver after finishing third in points. Graham raced the season while playing defensive end as a senior on the Liberty High School football team. His younger brother, Blayden Graham, plans to join him in a two-car USAC Western States Midget effort in 2027.

title: IndyCar Winner Christian Rasmussen to Make USAC Midget Debut at Turkey Night
text: The Danish driver will race the No. 98 Agajanian Special for Johnny Cofer and Dan Esslinger in the 85th Turkey Night Grand Prix, the USAC National Midget season finale, on Nov. 28 at Ventura Raceway. NTT IndyCar Series race winner Christian Rasmussen will make his USAC NOS…
body: The Danish driver will race the No. 98 Agajanian Special for Johnny Cofer and Dan Esslinger in the 85th Turkey Night Grand Prix, the USAC National Midget season finale, on Nov. 28 at Ventura Raceway. NTT IndyCar Series race winner Christian Rasmussen will make his USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midget debut in the 85th ARP Turkey Night Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov. 28, at Ventura Raceway in Ventura, California. The 26-year-old from Copenhagen, Denmark, drives the No. 21 Chevrolet for Ed Carpenter Racing in IndyCar, where he won for the first time at the Milwaukee Mile on Aug. 24, 2025. Rasmussen will drive the No. 98, a Spike short-arm chassis with an SR-11 engine fielded by car owner Johnny Cofer. With support from the Agajanian family, the car will carry a paint scheme based on the 1952 Agajanian Special that Troy Ruttman drove to victory in the Indianapolis 500. The entry reunites Cofer and Dan Esslinger, who won the 1994 USAC Western States Midget championship together with Cofer driving and Esslinger as owner. Cofer's daughter, Maria Cofer, has raced the same car. "I'm excited to try something that is completely out of my wheelhouse," Rasmussen said. "But most of all, I'm excited to get to work with Johnny Cofer and Dan Esslinger." Esslinger described it as a one-race deal for now. Rasmussen won the USF2000 title in 2020, the Indy Pro 2000 title in 2021 and the INDY NXT title in 2023. He also won the LMP2 class at the 2024 Rolex 24 at Daytona. Practice for Turkey Night is Friday, Nov. 27. Qualifying, heat races and the 98-lap main event are Saturday, Nov. 28, and the race will stream on FloRacing.

body: The Lemoore, Calif., driver will stay with Todd Carlile’s team for a third straight season on the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series. Cole Macedo will return to TwoC Racing’s No. 2C for the 2027 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season, sprintcarunlimited.com reported on Nov. 7 during the World Finals at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Macedo has not yet won a World of Outlaws feature; his career totals with the series stand at 180 starts, 19 top fives and 63 top 10s. Macedo joined TwoC Racing for 2025, with 2020 Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year Wayne Johnson moving from driver to crew chief on the No. 2C, according to the World of Outlaws. In April 2026, the series reported the team had recovered from multiple crashes at Kennedale Speedway Park to post a run of strong finishes, including a front-row start alongside his older brother, Carson Macedo, at US 36 Raceway. title: Nov 4: Cale Coons Named 2026 USAC National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year
text: Cale Coons of Greencastle, Indiana, earned the 2026 USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Championship Max Papis Innovations Rookie of the Year after a full-time debut that included his first series feature win. Coons, the 17-year-old son of USAC Triple Crown champion Jerry Coons Jr.,…
body: Cale Coons of Greencastle, Indiana, earned the 2026 USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Championship Max Papis Innovations Rookie of the Year after a full-time debut that included his first series feature win. Coons, the 17-year-old son of USAC Triple Crown champion Jerry Coons Jr., finished 11th in the national points in the Dooling Autosports-Curb-Agajanian No. 63. He scored one feature win, four top-fives, 23 top-10s, 32 laps led and a series-leading 16 heat victories. He is the first son of a past USAC National Sprint Car champion to win the series Rookie of the Year award, according to a USAC media release carried by FloRacing. His breakthrough came at Kokomo Speedway’s Sprint Car Smackdown. After finishing third on opening night, Coons led 29 of 30 laps the following night for his first USAC National Sprint Car win. Thomas Meseraull briefly took the lead after Coons’ early run up front; Coons slid back by one lap later and held on. He is the first USAC National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year to also win a feature in the same season since Emerson Axsom in 2022. Coons and Jerry Coons Jr. became the 10th father-son duo to each win a USAC National Sprint Car main event as drivers. Coons contested all 48 USAC National Sprint Car events in 2026, missing the feature transfer only twice. One of those nights, at Bloomington during Indiana Sprint Week, he used a provisional, started 25th and finished seventh — a plus-18 that ranked as the second-biggest feature advance of the season. He also finished second in the Bomb City 40 at Route 66 Motor Speedway in Amarillo, Texas, and collected three Rod End Supply Hard Charger awards earlier in the year.

title: Kyle Cummins Seeking Ownership Partners for 2027 USAC Return
text: The two-time and defending USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car champion is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the championship-winning team together after Petty Performance Racing ends its national program. Kyle Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership…
body: The two-time and defending USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car champion is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the championship-winning team together after Petty Performance Racing ends its national program. Kyle Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership opportunities to keep his championship-winning national sprint car team intact and return to the USAC AMSOIL Sprint Car National Tour in 2027, according to a Nov. 5, 2026 Kyle Cummins Racing update. The move follows Petty Performance Racing’s decision to conclude its involvement in the national sprint car program after back-to-back titles with Cummins. Jerry Petty and his wife, Bev, are stepping away from the national program to devote more time to family. In a post-season interview with USAC Racing, Petty said the future of the USAC National team would be up to Cummins, and that Petty Performance Racing would not continue the national program into 2027. USAC’s 2026 season review similarly reported that the Petty Performance Racing national team was shutting down and would not continue next year. Petty has entrusted Cummins with guiding the team’s next chapter. Cummins, of Princeton, Indiana, won the 2025 and 2026 USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car titles in the Petty Performance Racing No. 3p. In 2026 he led the series with 11 wins, 351 laps led, 35 top-fives and 45 top-10s in 48 feature starts, according to USAC. Across the two-year run with Petty Performance Racing, Cummins recorded 21 wins, 73 top-fives and 89 top-10s in 97 starts. The Nov. 5 update outlines a plan to preserve the winning formula: retain core crew members Cameron LaRose, Kasey DeRenzy and Zach Fields, with Cummins continuing as the driver. Those three were identified by USAC as core team members during the 2026 championship season. Possible paths include a complete team acquisition, a new ownership structure, strategic investment or long-term corporate sponsorship; terms were described as open. title: Steven Drevicki Wins Sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Car Title
text: The Reading, Pennsylvania driver claimed his record-extending sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship, 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno. Steven Drevicki of Reading, Pennsylvania won his record-extending sixth career USAC East Coast Sprint…
body: The Reading, Pennsylvania driver claimed his record-extending sixth USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship, 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno. Steven Drevicki of Reading, Pennsylvania won his record-extending sixth career USAC East Coast Sprint Cars Presented by Baer Den Farms championship in 2026. The 35-year-old closed out the closest points race in series history, finishing 28 points ahead of Christian Bruno of Deptford, New Jersey, 847-819. The previous closest title fight was 44 points in the series’ inaugural 2018 season, also won by Drevicki. All six of Drevicki’s titles have come in his own No. 19. He won the first three series championships in 2018, 2019 and 2020, then completed a second three-peat in 2024, 2025 and 2026. He recorded two feature victories, both at Bridgeport Motorsports Park in New Jersey, a series-high 11 top-five finishes, and top-10 results in all 12 of his feature starts. After chasing the point lead for much of the season, he took over the top spot from Bruno with three races remaining and closed with a fourth, a win and a sixth in his final three starts. Drevicki credited a midseason stretch of top-five finishes in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, including a wire-to-wire win at Bridgeport in August in which he led all 25 laps. In a September return to Bridgeport, he slid J.R. Fulper for the lead in a three-car battle with two laps remaining; Fulper’s car then began to stumble without fuel. “It’s wild to think about six,” Drevicki said. “I don’t know that it’s even sunk in.” Five drivers won USAC East Coast features in 2026: Bruno, Briggs Danner, Drevicki, Kenny Miller III and Chelby Hinton. Bruno led the series with five victories — Big Diamond Speedway in May, a three-race sweep at Selinsgrove Speedway, and Port Royal Speedway in September — and also led the tour in laps led (69) and heat-race wins (7). He finished second in the standings for the second time in the last three years. Miller was third, Kyle Spence fourth and Joe Kata fifth, both Spence and Kata posting their best career series points finishes. Olivia Thayer was named Rookie of the Year. Four drivers started all 12 features: Bruno, Drevicki, Kata and Miller.

body: Drake Edwards passed Cade Lewis just before the midpoint of the 30-lap feature at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Oct. 5, 2024. Lewis finished third and won the series championship by 11 points. Drake Edwards of Surprise, Arizona won the Avanti Windows & Doors USAC Western States Midget season finale on Oct. 5, 2024 at The Dirt Track at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway in Bakersfield, California. Edwards passed Cade Lewis just before the midpoint of the 30-lap feature for his second series victory of the season and also earned Rookie of the Year honors with a runner-up finish in the final points. Ben Worth of Coalinga, California led the first seven laps from the outside of the front row before Edwards slid in front in turn two on lap eight. Contact between those two allowed Lewis to drive from third to first. Lewis led laps eight and nine on the bottom before Edwards used the high side to lead lap 10. Sparks and a ball of flame then came from the back of Edwards’ car as he got on the brakes in turns one and two, and Lewis led laps 11 and 12. Edwards drove around the outside of Lewis off turn two to retake the lead for good on lap 13. Jett Yantis of Bakersfield, the night’s fast qualifier, passed Lewis for second and challenged Edwards on the final lap, but a slide-job attempt entering turn three was stifled when ninth-place Kyle Hawse occupied the low line. Edwards held on for the win. Yantis finished second, Lewis third, Brandt Twitty fourth and Dane Culver fifth. Worth, who led the opening seven laps, retired after an incident in turns one and two. Lewis, of Bakersfield, won the series driving championship by 11 points over Edwards, 622-611, the first title of his career. The result also gave car owner Dean Alexander of New Zealand his first series entrant championship. Edwards started fourth in the Petty Performance Racing No. 3p and also won the first heat.

title: Daison Pursley Won the Last Hangtown 100 and Is Already a USAC Midget Champion at 22
text: The Locust Grove, Okla., driver won the most recent Hangtown 100, the opener of USAC’s California midget swing, five years after a crash that left him paralyzed from the neck down. The USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets finish the 2026 season with seven races in California,…
body: The Locust Grove, Okla., driver won the most recent Hangtown 100, the opener of USAC’s California midget swing, five years after a crash that left him paralyzed from the neck down. The USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets finish the 2026 season with seven races in California, the Golden State Invasion, starting with the Hangtown 100 at Placerville Speedway on Nov. 13-14. The swing continues at Plaza Park Raceway in Visalia on Nov. 18, the track’s first date on the series schedule, then the Chase Johnson Classic at Merced Speedway on Nov. 20-21, the Jason Leffler Memorial at Bakersfield Speedway at Kevin Harvick’s Kern Raceway on Nov. 24 and the 85th Turkey Night Grand Prix at Ventura Raceway on Nov. 28, according to USAC’s schedule . The most recent Hangtown 100, in 2025, was won by Daison Pursley of Locust Grove, Okla., who turned 22 on Oct. 20. The 2024 edition was canceled for rain and cold. Pursley started fourth in a 25-car field on Nov. 15, 2025, and stayed in the top four for all 100 laps. On lap 96 he was second and tried to pass leader Kyle Larson in turn one; Pursley’s car appeared to clip the infield berm and slid into Larson’s, which flipped. Pursley finished 0.257 seconds ahead of Steven Snyder Jr. for $20,000, USAC reported . He apologized afterward and said he had not wanted to win that way. The win was one entry on a long USAC list. Pursley won the National Midget championship in 2024 with CB Industries and the Indiana Midget Week title the same year, and he was the 2023 National Sprint Car Rookie of the Year, the 2023 and 2024 National Passing Master champion and the 2017 National Micro Sprint champion, according to USAC’s driver page . That page, last updated on Jan. 1, 2026, credits him with 11 National Midget wins in 136 starts through 2025, seven of them in 2024. At the 2025 4-Crown Nationals at Eldora Speedway he won the National Sprint Car, National Midget and Silver Crown features in one night, joining Jack Hewitt, Larson and Logan Seavey as the fourth driver to do so. His career nearly ended at 17. A crash at Arizona Speedway in November 2021 broke his neck, and he was diagnosed as an incomplete quadriplegic. After surgery and rehabilitation at the Shepherd Center in Atlanta, he attended the 2022 Chili Bowl Nationals in Tulsa that January, returned to racing in August 2022 and was back in victory lane that September, according to KJRH and FloRacing . He finished second to Larson in the 2025 Chili Bowl Nationals and sixth in the 2026 A-feature. Pursley has also moved into winged sprint cars. He won at Lernerville Speedway on Sept. 13, 2025, and was named the High Limit Racing Rookie of the Year driving for Buch Motorsports. In October 2025 Kasey Kahne Racing hired him as its full-time driver of the No. 9 for 2026, after Brad Sweet stepped away from full-time touring, FloRacing reported , and Placerville Speedway’s preview for this week’s race calls him a High Limit regular. On Sept. 26, 2026, he led all 50 laps in the USAC Silver Crown feature at the 4-Crown Nationals, the debut of the Spire Motorsports/CB Industries Silver Crown team, for his fifth career 4-Crown win as a driver, Speed Sport reported .

title: From Speedcar Champion to Two-Time WA Sprintcar Champion: Dayne Kingshott’s Rise With Krikke Motorsport
text: The Bunbury driver won his second Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at his team’s home track, four seasons after his first and nearly eight years after winning the Australian Speedcar Championship. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar…
body: The Bunbury driver won his second Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at his team’s home track, four seasons after his first and nearly eight years after winning the Australian Speedcar Championship. Dayne Kingshott won the Western Australian Sprintcar Championship on Nov. 7, 2026, at Bunbury Speedway, leading every lap of the 35-lap feature after starting second, according to Auto Action . It was his second state title, Krikke Motorsport’s ninth and the team’s first win of the 2026-27 season. Callum Williamson finished second, Kaiden Manders third, Kris Coyle fourth and Daniel Harding fifth. The race was round three of the Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series, and Speedway Illustrated News reported in July that it was the first time in some while the event had been run at the South West venue. Kingshott, who drives the WA No. 2 Mobil 1/Bunbury Toyota-backed Maxim, said the win meant more because it was the team’s first together at Bunbury, where many of its sponsors are local, the team said . His route to the title began in speedcars. The Bunbury resident won the Australian Speedcar Championship at Perth Motorplex on Feb. 9, 2019, ahead of Adam Clarke of New South Wales and American Jason McDougal. He moved to 410 Sprintcars with Krikke Motorsport for 2020-21, when pandemic travel restrictions kept Kerry Madsen from driving the team’s car, and finished second in the SEG Series standings that season, according to the team’s history page . He won his first 410 Sprintcar feature with the team in 2021-22, along with the Perth Motorplex Track Championship. His first state title came on Dec. 3, 2022, in the 61st running of the event at Perth Motorplex. Starting third, Kingshott took the lead from James Inglis with about six laps to go in a 35-lap feature that took more than an hour because of repeated stoppages, and finished ahead of Taylor Milling and Inglis. Krikke Motorsport called it the team’s eighth Western Australian title, following Ron Krikke in 1983-84 and 1984-85, John Krikke in 1988-89, Brooke Tatnell in 2013-14, Jamie Veal in 2017-18 and Madsen in 2018-19 and 2019-20. The state titles sit beside a run of consistent seasons. Kingshott won the Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series in 2023-24 with 2,820 points, the first series championship for Krikke Motorsport, after finishing second, third and fourth in the previous three seasons. He repeated in 2024-25 with 3,222 points, 52 ahead of Williamson, and won a third series title in 2025-26 with six round wins. In November 2025 he became the first driver to win the King of Wings three years in a row, beating James McFadden by 0.010 seconds at Perth Motorplex. In December, at the 2025 High Limit International at Perth Motorplex, he finished second to Kyle Larson in the $110,000-to-win race. Among Western Australian champions, Kingshott now has two titles. Perth Motorplex credits Alf Barbagallo, known as “Mr. Sprintcar,” with six, and the Sprintcar World honour roll, which begins in 2009, lists Jason Kendrick (2011, 2014 and 2021) and Madsen (2010, 2018 and 2019) with three each. Kingshott sits seventh in the 2026-27 series standings, and Krikke Motorsport has said it is aiming for a fourth Maddington Toyota Sprintcar Series championship. The next round is the King of Wings at Perth Motorplex on Nov. 14, where Kingshott is the three-time defending winner.

title: Emerson Axsom Follows Chili Bowl Win With World of Outlaws Rookie of the Year Title
text: The Franklin, Ind., driver won the Golden Driller in January, took his first World of Outlaws feature in September and closed his first full-time season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year. Emerson Axsom finished his first full-time World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint…
body: The Franklin, Ind., driver won the Golden Driller in January, took his first World of Outlaws feature in September and closed his first full-time season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year. Emerson Axsom finished his first full-time World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season as the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year presented by Five Star Bodies, an award announced at the series’ awards celebration on Nov. 8 in Charlotte, N.C. ( our banquet report ). The year began with a win in the Chili Bowl Nationals, a crown jewel, and included his first series feature victory. World of Outlaws statistics credit Axsom and the Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports No. 27 with one win, 11 top-five finishes, 32 top 10s and 66 laps led, and the series’ points table lists him ninth with 8,946 points. Axsom won the 40th Chili Bowl Nationals on Jan. 17 in Tulsa, Okla., driving the No. 39A for Kevin Swindell’s team. Swindell, a four-time Chili Bowl winner as a driver, had messaged him on Instagram the previous summer to ask if he wanted the ride, NASCAR.com reported. Starting second in the 55-lap A-feature, Axsom passed pole-sitter Kyle Larson, the 2025 winner, on the fourth lap. On lap 16 Larson flipped after contact with the slowed car of C.J. Leary and was eliminated, and Axsom held the lead through challenges from Logan Seavey and Justin Grant. A late caution for Grant’s flip in turn three set up a green-white-checkered finish, and Axsom held off Kevin Thomas Jr., who had started 18th, to win. Hank Davis was third, Seavey fourth and Briggs Danner fifth, according to the official results. The win followed several seasons of moving between divisions. According to the World of Outlaws, Axsom ran the USAC National Midget Series in 2021 and USAC National Sprint Cars in 2022 and 2023, then committed fully to winged sprint cars in 2024 with Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports, winning that year at Lincoln Park Speedway and Knoxville Raceway. He was the Knoxville Nationals Rookie of the Year in 2024 and won his first All Star Circuit of Champions feature at Eldora Speedway in 2025. In July 2025 he filled in for two months in the KCP Racing No. 18 after Giovanni Scelzi and the team separated, then returned to the Klaasmeyer/Petry car. On Feb. 3, 2026, the series announced he would run the full World of Outlaws schedule in the No. 27 for car owners Dale Klaasmeyer and Scott Petry. His father, Joe Axsom, serves as crew chief. The season started slowly. Axsom had no top 10s in his first six races, then finished second at Tri-State Speedway in Haubstadt, Ind., on April 19, his best result of the year at that point. That finish moved him 28 points ahead of Ashton Torgerson in the rookie standings, the World of Outlaws reported. His first win came Sept. 6 at Huset’s Speedway in Brandon, S.D., in the L.G. Everist Huset’s Shootout finale. Starting second in the 40-lap feature, he traded the lead with Carson Macedo and held off David Gravel and Michael Kofoid on late restarts for a $25,000 payday. The series listed him as its 160th different feature winner, the fifth first-time winner of 2026 and the 21st different winner of the season. Axsom was strong through the second half. Before the World Finals, the World of Outlaws noted he had 19 top 10s in his previous 23 races. At The Dirt Track at Charlotte he won Thursday’s C-main to qualify for the feature, started 25th and finished 22nd. He was 12th on Friday and 18th on Saturday, qualifying for all three A-mains. Under the Five Star Bodies program announced by the World of Outlaws in February, the sprint car Rookie of the Year receives a new body and a $10,000 bonus. The 2027 World of Outlaws season opens Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park in Barberville, Fla.

title: Kyle Larson Returns to Placerville With Four Hangtown 100 Wins and a Co-Promoter’s Stake
text: The Elk Grove, Calif., driver has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville — the inaugural 100-lapper in 2019, a preliminary feature in 2021, and both nights in 2023 — and enters the Nov. 13-14, 2026 running as co-promoter, racing both a midget and a…
body: The Elk Grove, Calif., driver has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville — the inaugural 100-lapper in 2019, a preliminary feature in 2021, and both nights in 2023 — and enters the Nov. 13-14, 2026 running as co-promoter, racing both a midget and a 360 sprint car. Kyle Larson goes into the Hangtown 100 at Placerville Speedway on Nov. 13-14, 2026, entered in both the USAC NOS Energy Drink National Midgets and winged 360 sprint cars on each day, FloRacing reported . He arrives five days after clinching his third NASCAR Cup Series championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Nov. 8, according to NASCAR.com and NBC Sports . The Hangtown 100 is the only 100-lap USAC National Midget main event on the 2026 schedule and opens the series’ seven-race Golden State Invasion in California, USAC said . Larson has four Hangtown 100 USAC National Midget feature wins at Placerville Speedway, the official total on USAC’s 2025 event preview : Nov. 20, 2019; Nov. 19, 2021; and both nights in 2023, Nov. 17 and Nov. 19. The race debuted in 2019 under original promoter Matt Wood. On Nov. 20, 2019, Larson started 10th in a 28-car field, took the lead on lap 35 and led the final 66 laps, finishing 8.152 seconds ahead of Christopher Bell. He earned $20,000 for the 100-lap feature and a $12,000 bonus as the event’s overall points champion, a $32,000 total that USAC described as the richest event in the history of its National and Western States Midget divisions. In 2021 he won the Nov. 19 preliminary feature, and Justin Grant won the 100-lap finale the next night. Buddy Kofoid won the 100-lapper in 2022. The 2024 edition was canceled because of rain and cold. In 2023 he swept both features. The Friday opener was a 30-lap race that he led from lap 6 and finished in 6 minutes, 14.69 seconds without a caution. On Sunday, Nov. 19, he started 16th after the random draw gave the points leader that spot, passed Logan Seavey for the lead on lap 93 and won by 0.881 seconds. USAC reported that he became the first two-time winner of the 100-lapper and the first driver to win a second overall Hangtown 100 points championship, for a $25,500 weekend. The Sunday win was his 27th in the USAC National Midget Series, tying Gary Bettenhausen and Tony Stewart for 15th on the all-time list. Larson became co-promoter in October 2025, when Russell Motorsports announced the partnership. That year’s Friday opener was washed out by nearly 3.5 inches of rain, leaving one program on Saturday, Nov. 15. Larson set fast time, started 11th, took the lead on lap 44 and led a race-high 52 laps. On lap 96, Daison Pursley, who had moved into second, tried to pass for the lead in turn one, and contact sent Larson’s car flipping. Larson finished 15th and Pursley won, USAC reported . Pursley apologized afterward and said he had not wanted to win that way, and Larson called it a bummer but said he understood the move. Placerville has been part of Larson’s career since his teens. He made his first sprint car start at the track in 2007 and won there that August at age 15, becoming the youngest feature winner in the speedway’s history at the time, according to a contemporary Civil War Series report. He also clinched the 2010 Golden State KWS-NARC Series championship there. This year the Hangtown 100 adds winged 360 sprint cars on both days for the first time as a companion class, with $2,000 to win each night, and racing starts at 2 p.m. PT with gates opening at 1 p.m., the track said .

text: David Gravel finished sixth in Thursday’s World Finals feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte to clinch his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series title. David Gravel clinched his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car…
body: David Gravel finished sixth in Thursday’s World Finals feature at The Dirt Track at Charlotte to clinch his third consecutive World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series title. Gravel, driving the Big Game Motorsports No. 2, started fifth and finished sixth in the 25-lap feature won by Rico Abreu. That finish locked up the title. Gravel and Big Game Motorsports won their first title together in 2024 and repeated in 2025. Gravel entered the World Finals with a 124-point lead over Michael “Buddy” Kofoid, according to official World of Outlaws standings. Before Thursday’s feature, Gravel posted on social media that a top-16 finish would secure the championship. Abreu won Thursday’s feature ahead of Tyler Courtney and Bill Balog, with Kofoid fourth and Garet Williamson fifth. title: Nov 2: Gravel Eyes Historic Three-Peat at Charlotte World Finals
text: David Gravel and Big Game Motorsports hold a 124-point lead over Michael Kofoid heading into the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals (Nov. 4-7) at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. David Gravel enters the final week of the 2026 World of Outlaws Sprint Car Series season on…
body: David Gravel and Big Game Motorsports hold a 124-point lead over Michael Kofoid heading into the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals (Nov. 4-7) at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. David Gravel enters the final week of the 2026 World of Outlaws Sprint Car Series season on the verge of a rare achievement. Through 48 years of Series history, only three drivers have won three consecutive World of Outlaws championships: Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz and Brad Sweet. Gravel and the Big Game Motorsports team, which won its first title together in 2024 and repeated in 2025, can become the fourth at the Dave Smith Motors World of Outlaws World Finals, Nov. 4-7 at The Dirt Track at Charlotte in Concord, N.C. A third title would also tie Gravel with Sammy Swindell for the fourth-most championships in Series history. The lead has been built on consistency. Gravel and the Tod Quiring-owned No. 2 team have collected 11 wins, 32 podiums and 64 top-10 finishes across 72 starts this season, with an average finish of 5.17. He holds a 124-point advantage over Michael "Buddy" Kofoid of Roth Motorsports, who leads the Series with 17 wins. Sheldon Haudenschild sits third, 222 points back, followed by Carson Macedo at minus-320. Gravel's crew includes crew chief Cody Jacobs, car chief Luke Vaughn and tire specialist Zach Patterson. SPEED SPORT noted that the team's statistics dipped slightly compared with 2025, but the championship remains theirs to lose. The clinch scenario is straightforward. Three Sprint Car Series races remain on the 78-race schedule, all at Charlotte, according to World of Outlaws standings (75 of 78 races complete). Big Game Motorsports stated entering the week, as reported by Speedway Digest, that as long as Gravel finishes 20th or better in each of the three World Finals main events, he will clinch the title. If he falls outside the top 20 in any of the three features, the title would depend on Kofoid's and Haudenschild's results, and the Series has not published scenarios for that case. Charlotte has been one of Gravel's strongest tracks. His eight World of Outlaws wins at The Dirt Track at Charlotte are the second-most by any driver, and half of them have come since he joined Big Game Motorsports. In 14 Charlotte starts in the No. 2, he has finished fourth or better eight times. The four-night World Finals closes the Series' 49th season and also features the World of Outlaws Late Models and the Super DIRTcar Series.

title: Nov. 4, 1945: Kenny Weld Is Born in Kansas City
text: Kenny Weld won the Knoxville Nationals at 18, went on to win it four times, captured three Williams Grove National Opens and later built the “Batmobile” modified and the Weld Tech business. Kenneth Eugene Weld was born Nov. 4, 1945, in Kansas City, Missouri, into a racing…
body: Kenny Weld won the Knoxville Nationals at 18, went on to win it four times, captured three Williams Grove National Opens and later built the “Batmobile” modified and the Weld Tech business. Kenneth Eugene Weld was born Nov. 4, 1945, in Kansas City, Missouri, into a racing family. He started racing in 1961 at Riverside and Lakeside Speedways, moving from jalopies to sportsman cars and then to super modifieds in 1962, according to the Eastern Motorsport Press Association. In 1964, at 18, he won the Knoxville Nationals. Teamed with his father, Taylor “Pappy” Weld, in a car known as the “Tank,” he won the event again in 1965. He returned from Pennsylvania to win two more Nationals in 1972 and 1973 for car owner Bob Weikert, giving him four Knoxville Nationals titles in nine starts, according to The Third Turn. By the late 1960s Weld had moved east and became one of the leading outlaw sprint car drivers before the World of Outlaws formed in 1978. In 1970 he won 27 features and the Williams Grove championship in Bud Grimm’s car, and in 1974 he won 39 features and a record fifth Williams Grove championship, according to EMPA. The Third Turn credits him with three wins in seven starts in the Williams Grove National Open, along with a win in the Tuscarora 50. In 1975 he moved to big-block modifieds and won 16 races driving for Weikert at Reading. Weld’s influence extended to car building. In 1980 he built, with Don Brown, the modified known as the “Batmobile” for Gary Balough. Balough won at Syracuse with it, and the rules were changed to keep cars like it from racing again. Weld retired from driving after a crash at Buckeye Speedway in Ohio in 1988 and founded Weld Tech with his brother Greg and his daughter Debra; the business became known for cylinder-head porting. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1997 and died March 20, 1997, after a two-year battle with cancer. The Weld family is well represented in the Hall. Greg Weld, the 1963 Knoxville Nationals winner and 1967 USAC sprint car champion, was inducted in 1998, and Pappy Weld, who started the family’s open-wheel tradition by building and owning a midget in the 1930s, was inducted in 2006.

body: Cummins clinched the 2026 title Oct. 22 at Central Arizona Raceway with two races left. He won a career-high 11 features and finished 183 points ahead of Justin Grant. Kyle Cummins of Princeton, Indiana, won the 2026 USAC AMSOIL National Sprint Car championship, his second straight series title. He clinched it Oct. 22 with a third-place finish in the Western World Championships opener at Central Arizona Raceway in Casa Grande, Arizona, with two races left, USAC reported. The result also gave Petty Performance Racing its second straight entrant title with the No. 3p. Cummins finished with 3,333 points, 183 ahead of Justin Grant (3,150), according to USAC’s final standings. Mitchel Moles was third with 3,075, Jake Swanson fourth with 2,873 and Kevin Thomas Jr. fifth with 2,657. Cummins led the series with a career-high 11 wins and 351 laps led in 48 starts, and he tied Grant for the most top-10 finishes with 45. Cummins took the points lead in the eighth race of the season, in early April, and kept it the rest of the year. He set a USAC National Sprint Car record with 45 consecutive top-10 finishes, breaking the mark of 29 set by Thomas in 2025. His wins included his first USAC victories at the Terre Haute Action Track half-mile, in April’s Jim Hurtubise Classic; at Eldora Speedway, in May; and at Knoxville Raceway, in May’s Corn Belt Clash. He returned to Eldora in September to win the 4-Crown Nationals, and he also won the Indiana Sprint Week and Eastern Storm titles. “I think I’m more excited about this one than I was the first one,” Cummins told USAC. “I was always saying that just one would be cool. You can have a lucky year and it felt like everything went our way last year. To come out this year and back it up, I don’t know if everything went our way, but we definitely had a really good season.” Shortly after the final race, Petty Performance Racing announced its national team would shut down and not continue into 2027, USAC reported. Cummins is pursuing ownership and partnership options to keep the team together for 2027, DirtSprintCars.com reported Nov. 6 .

text: Mark Kinser held off Australian Peter Murphy to win the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic, the season finale of the 1998 Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series, as cousin Steve Kinser celebrated his 15th series championship. Mark Kinser won the 30-lap A-Feature of the inaugural…
body: Mark Kinser held off Australian Peter Murphy to win the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic, the season finale of the 1998 Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series, as cousin Steve Kinser celebrated his 15th series championship. Mark Kinser won the 30-lap A-Feature of the inaugural Channellock Fall Classic on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 1998, at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, the finale of the Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series’ 20th anniversary season, according to a series race report by Richard Day published by The Auto Channel. The victory, in the #5M Wirtgen Maxim, was Kinser’s 12th A-Feature win of the season, ran his winning streak to three and was his fourth straight victory at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, the report said. Peter Murphy finished second, followed by Sammy Swindell, Danny Lasoski and Steve Kinser, according to the report and The Third Turn’s event results. Kinser started on the pole after winning the Channellock Dash, his 14th dash win of the year, and led the first 17 laps, according to the report. Murphy, the Vivarin Fast-Time Award winner, started inside the fifth row, worked forward and passed Kinser for the lead late in lap 18. Murphy led through lap 25 before Kinser regained the lead and led the final five laps, finishing 3.608 seconds ahead. The report described Murphy’s runner-up finish as the best by an Australian driver in series history. “I wasn’t saving anything,” Kinser said, according to the report. “I changed my line on the last restart and I feel fortunate to be here.” The finale also marked the end of the championship chase. Steve Kinser’s Quaker State team celebrated his 15th Pennzoil World of Outlaws Series drivers’ championship at the track, and the report said he was the first driver/owner to win both titles in the same year. Earlier in the week, the Las Vegas Sun reported that Mark Kinser had won a Channellock Fall Classic A-Feature at the LVMS half-mile on Tuesday night, and that his 12th feature win of the season was not enough to overtake his cousin in the points standings. “Vegas has been really good to us,” Mark Kinser told the Sun. Tyler Nelson of Olathe, Kansas successfully defended his USAC Midwest Thunder SpeeD2 Midget championship in 2026. This year he won at all three tracks and quadrupled his career win total from one to four. In May at Williamsburg, Ohio’s Moler Raceway Park, he led all 25 laps in wire-to-wire fashion and won by 6.054 seconds. In September at Putnamville, Indiana’s Lincoln Park Speedway, he went from fifth to first in the next-to-last race and took the point lead for good. Nelson locked up the title with a fifth-place finish in the October finale at Montpelier Speedway. He became the third driver in the 11-year history of the series to win consecutive championships, following Aaron Leffel (2017, 2018 and 2019) and Jacob Denney (2020 and 2021). The point lead had changed hands among Nelson, Matt Lux and Massingill for much of the season. Massingill finished in the top three of the standings for the sixth year in a row and was the runner-up in 2026. The series’ all-time winningest driver, with 23 victories, added five more wins in the latter half of the year — two at Moler, plus Millstream, Circle City and Montpelier — after a 364-night winless stretch, and led a series-high 96 laps. Lux finished third. Kole Kirkman was named Rookie of the Year after finishing sixth. title: Sam Hafertepe Jr. Wins Record Seventh ASCS National Tour Title
text: Hafertepe clinched the 2026 title Oct. 17 by winning the Fuzzy’s Fall Fling finale at Creek County Speedway with a last-lap pass. He beat Matt Covington by 41 points. After the season, he announced he will join Jess Jordan Motorsports in 2027 and shift his focus to selected 410…
body: Hafertepe clinched the 2026 title Oct. 17 by winning the Fuzzy’s Fall Fling finale at Creek County Speedway with a last-lap pass. He beat Matt Covington by 41 points. After the season, he announced he will join Jess Jordan Motorsports in 2027 and shift his focus to selected 410 World of Outlaws and High Limit starts. Sam Hafertepe Jr. of Sunnyvale, Texas, won the 2026 American Sprint Car Series National Tour championship, his seventh series title and the most in ASCS history. He clinched it Oct. 17 at Creek County Speedway in Sapulpa, Oklahoma, by winning the 40-lap Fuzzy’s Fall Fling season finale with a pass for the lead on the last lap, ASCS reported. Hafertepe entered the finale with a 21-point lead over Matt Covington and started eighth. He passed Covington for third with 14 laps left, got by Alex Sewell for second with two laps to go and took the lead from Garrett Benson in Turns 3 and 4 on the final lap. Benson finished second, Sewell third, Covington fourth and Steven Shebester fifth. Hafertepe won the title by 41 points over Covington. The win was Hafertepe’s seventh of 2026 and the 95th ASCS National Tour feature win of his career. He made 27 feature starts this season with 19 top-five and 21 top-10 finishes, according to ASCS season statistics. His first five titles came in consecutive seasons from 2016 to 2020, and his sixth, in 2025, moved him past Jason Johnson for the most in series history. Hafertepe and car owner Miles Hill won both the driver and owner championships with the Hill’s Racing Team No. 15H. “I owe it all to Miles and this team,” Hafertepe said at the ASCS awards banquet Oct. 18 in Tulsa. “For the last nine years, you’ve given us everything we need. This team never wavered this entire year, and as a driver, it’s the best kind of ownership you can have.” Covington finished second in points and Seth Bergman third. Hafertepe collected $40,000 from the series points fund. The 2027 ASCS National Tour season opens Feb. 4-6 at Volusia Speedway Park during the DIRTcar Nationals. After the season, a Jess Jordan Motorsports press release dated Oct. 20 said Hafertepe will join the newly formed, Texas-based team for 2027, concluding a partnership of nearly a decade with Hill’s Racing. The release said he will shift his focus from 360 to 410 sprint car racing and that his schedule will include selected World of Outlaws and High Limit events, with 2027 serving as a building year toward the long-term goal of competing on a national tour. Further details on the 2027 schedule will be announced later, the release said. Hafertepe posted the release on Oct. 21. Brody Brown, who was Hafertepe’s head mechanic this past season at 17 years old, will join him at Jess Jordan Motorsports, the release said. The partnership with Miles Hill and Hill’s Racing produced five ASCS National Tour championships and more than 80 feature victories, according to the release.

Tanner Holmes chased him home in second. Charlotte got a fresh dose of Hot Sauce on Friday night. Cameron Smith and Buddy Schweibinz completed the top five. David Gravel, already the 2026 champion, was ninth. The win makes Scelzi the 24th different World of Outlaws winner in 2026, one shy of the record for most in a season with one night remaining. It's his 11th career WoO victory. Scelzi noted the cushion got lipped up after the till, but credited the track crew and fans who stuck around for nearly 12 hours. Winning in Spire's home state with the Chili's car was a nice bonus — seven years since his last Charlotte triumph. The World Finals wrap Saturday with the $25,000-to-win season finale. Jack Wagner of Lone Jack, Missouri won the 2026 USAC Wholesale Batteries Midwest Racing Association Sprint Car championship. USAC noted it was his best season driving a non-winged sprint car. He won more races across all divisions in 2026 (10) than he had in the previous five seasons combined (8). Ricky Lewis won two of his three series starts, including April’s season opener at Springfield Raceway on a last-lap pass of Braydon Cromwell. Wyatt Burks passed Wagner with two laps remaining to win August’s Weld Memorial at Lakeside. Tom Curran collected his first career sprint car win after passing Wagner in June at Valley, and Wesley Smith passed Wagner with two laps remaining to win in May at Valley. Burks finished third in the standings, just ahead of Wagner’s brother, Samuel Wagner, with Cromwell fifth. Ten drivers started all 12 points-paying features, including both Wagners, Howard, Burks and Cromwell.

title: World of Outlaws Set Eight 2027 Pennsylvania Dates, Opening May 12 at Lincoln
text: The series will face the PA Posse in eight races at Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway and BAPS Motor Speedway, from the Gettysburg Clash on May 12 to the 65th National Open on Oct. 1-2. The World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series will race eight times in…
body: The series will face the PA Posse in eight races at Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway and BAPS Motor Speedway, from the Gettysburg Clash on May 12 to the 65th National Open on Oct. 1-2. The World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series will race eight times in Pennsylvania in 2027, the series announced Nov. 12. The dates are spread over three tracks: Lincoln Speedway, Williams Grove Speedway in Mechanicsburg and BAPS Motor Speedway in York Haven. According to World of Outlaws, the series won five of the eight Pennsylvania races against the PA Posse in 2026, and Posse drivers won three. The swing opens Wednesday, May 12, with the Gettysburg Clash at Lincoln Speedway. Buddy Kofoid and Roth Motorsports have won the last two runnings of the race, the series said. The series then moves to Williams Grove for the HVAC Distributors Morgan Cup on Friday and Saturday, May 14-15. In 2026, Kasey Kahne won the Morgan Cup opener for his first World of Outlaws win, and David Gravel won the finale, according to World of Outlaws. Three summer races follow. The Bricker’s Bash is set for Thursday, July 29, at BAPS Motor Speedway, where Chase Dietz won for the Posse in 2026. Williams Grove then hosts the C&D Rigging Summer Nationals on July 30-31. Kofoid and Gravel won the two 2026 Summer Nationals races, the series said. The Pennsylvania schedule ends with the 65th J&S Classics National Open at Williams Grove on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 1-2. In 2026, Gravel won the opening night and Dietz won the National Open title and $75,000, according to World of Outlaws. The series said ticket information for the Pennsylvania races will be announced later. The 2027 World of Outlaws season begins Feb. 10-13 with the Federated Auto Parts DIRTcar Nationals at Volusia Speedway Park in Barberville, Florida, according to the series.

body: Kyle Ripper was named Crew Chief of the Year and received the NOS Energy Drink Eloy Gutierrez Spirit Award. Sheldon Haudenschild was voted Most Popular Driver, and Emerson Axsom was named Rookie of the Year. Kyle Ripper received two honors Sunday night, Nov. 8, at the 2026 World of Outlaws Awards Celebration in Charlotte, N.C., the night after the World Finals closed the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series season. Ripper, crew chief for Sheldon Haudenschild on the KCP Racing entry, was named the series’ Crew Chief of the Year and also received the NOS Energy Drink Eloy Gutierrez Spirit Award , according to the World of Outlaws. The series described Ripper as Haudenschild’s longtime crew chief and said he “continues to be entirely dedicated to Sprint Car Racing and the World of Outlaws.” Haudenschild was named the 2026 World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Most Popular Driver , an award decided by fan voting, according to the series. Emerson Axsom received the Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year award presented by Five Star Bodies. Axsom opened 2026 by winning the Chili Bowl Nationals and earned his first World of Outlaws feature win Sept. 6 at Huset’s Speedway in the Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports No. 27. Series statistics credit him with one win, 11 top-five finishes and 32 top-10s in 70 feature starts this season. Announcer Johnny Gibson received the Ted Johnson Award after his 30th season calling World of Outlaws Sprint Car races. “I’m the luckiest Sprint Car fan in the world,” Gibson said in a video posted by the series. Ace Pruitt of Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing was named the Jason Johnson Sportsman of the Year . Brian Morrison was again named Engine Builder of the Year ; the series noted that Morrison Racing Engines powers Big Game Motorsports and KCP Racing, the teams that finished first and third in the 2026 standings. The banquet followed David Gravel’s official crowning Saturday night at The Dirt Track at Charlotte. Gravel won his third consecutive World of Outlaws championship with Big Game Motorsports, finishing the season with 11 wins, 48 top-five finishes and 66 top-10s in 75 starts, according to the series. He joins Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz and Brad Sweet as the only drivers to win at least three straight series titles. The 2027 season opens Feb. 10-13 at Volusia Speedway Park.

title: Steve Kinser “The King”
text: World of Outlaws. Steve Kinser is the winningest driver in World of Outlaws history, with 20 WoO championships and 690 feature wins. "The King" won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title, a record 12 Knoxville Nationals and seven Kings Royals. Steve Kinser built the World of Outlaws…
body: Steve Kinser is the winningest driver in World of Outlaws history, with 20 WoO championships and 690 feature wins. "The King" won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title, a record 12 Knoxville Nationals and seven Kings Royals. Steve Kinser built the World of Outlaws into a national institution as much as any promoter did. Arriving for the series' first season in 1978, the Bloomington, Indiana, driver and his cousin Karl Kinser's team set the standard every touring sprint car program has chased since, and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame later named him sprint car racing's greatest driver of the century. He won the inaugural 1978 Outlaws title and 20 series championships in all. His 690 World of Outlaws A-feature wins are nearly 300 more than anyone else, a margin unmatched in American motorsports. Kinser owned the sport's crown jewels. He won the Knoxville Nationals a record 12 times and the Kings Royal at Eldora seven times, the National Open at Williams Grove four times (1990, 1992, 1994 and 2003), and among the majors he won the Gold Cup Race of Champions at Chico more than ten times. His 1987 season remains the benchmark. He won 46 Outlaws features that year, including 24 of the final 26. Kinser was versatile beyond the dirt. He won the 1994 IROC race at Talladega, started the 1995 Daytona 500 and drove in the 1997 Indianapolis 500. He briefly left the Outlaws for the National Sprint Tour in 2006, returned in 2007, and retired from sprint car racing in 2016. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2005 and the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2017. body: Sammy Swindell is a three-time World of Outlaws champion (1981, 1982, 1997) whose 394 WoO feature wins rank second all-time. He also won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals, three Kings Royals and five Chili Bowl Midget Nationals, and in 1997 he became the first owner-driver to win the Outlaws title. Sammy Swindell was the engineer of the modern sprint car as much as its driver. A technically minded Tennessean from a racing family, he was one of the Memphis-area group that helped make the early World of Outlaws, and alongside Steve Kinser and Doug Wolfgang he is remembered as one of the "Big Three" of winged sprint car racing. He won Outlaws championships in 1981 and 1982. In 1997 he won a third title in his own car, becoming the first owner-driver to win the WoO crown. He was also runner-up four times, and his 394 World of Outlaws A-main wins rank second all-time. Swindell won the 1983 Knoxville Nationals and the Kings Royal in 1992, 1999 and 2012. In 1981 he took the wing off to win the Pacific Coast Nationals at Ascot. In midgets he won the Chili Bowl five times: 1989, 1992, 1996, 1998 and 2009. Swindell also tested himself elsewhere. He made CART starts in 1985 and 1986, failed to qualify for the 1987 Indianapolis 500, and ran the inaugural 1995 NASCAR Truck Series season, finishing 12th in points. body: Doug Wolfgang of Sioux Falls, South Dakota, is a five-time Knoxville Nationals champion with 140 World of Outlaws feature wins, fifth-most all-time. He was one of the "Big Three" of the early Outlaws era, and he also won two Kings Royals and 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races. Doug Wolfgang carried the Midwest's homegrown sprint car scene onto the national stage. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota, driver came up in super modifieds and, with car owner Bob Trostle, broke through at Knoxville in the mid-1970s before becoming one of the "Big Three" of the early World of Outlaws era. Wolfgang won the Knoxville Nationals five times, in 1977, 1978, 1984, 1985 and 1989. He won them for four different owners: Trostle, Bill Smith, Bob Weikert and Danny Peace. With the Outlaws he finished second in the standings four times and won 140 features, fifth-most in series history. He also won 37 All Star Circuit of Champions races and two Kings Royals. On April 3, 1992, a fiery crash at Lakeside Speedway in Kansas City left him with burns over about 30 percent of his body and a broken vertebra. He came back to win an IMCA 360 sprint championship and the 1996 ASCS 360 Nationals, then retired in 1997 after another serious crash. body: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500. Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series. Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500. He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame. body: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive. He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash. Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown. He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014. title: Mel Kenyon “King of the Midgets”

body: Mel Kenyon, the "King of the Midgets," holds the USAC National Midget record with 111 feature wins and seven championships between 1964 and 1985. He won those races after losing the fingers of his left hand in a 1965 crash, and he made eight Indianapolis 500 starts. Mel Kenyon and his brother Don built a family midget operation that set the standard in USAC National Midget racing. Don was his car owner and crew chief, and they also built their own chassis. From 2004 to 2009 their Kenyon Midget Series ran under USAC sanction. Mel won 111 USAC National Midget races, the series record. He won seven national championships over 21 years: 1964, 1967, 1968, 1974, 1977, 1981 and 1985. He also won at least one race in 21 straight seasons, 1962 through 1982. Most of that came after a fiery 1965 champ car crash at Langhorne that burned off the fingers of his left hand. The brothers designed a special glove that fit over a stud on the steering wheel so he could steer with his palm. Kenyon made eight Indianapolis 500 starts and finished in the top five in half of them, with a best of third in 1968. He retired in 2009 after more than 50 years of midget racing and 925 USAC National Midget starts. 111 USAC National Midget wins (record) 7 USAC National Midget titles 7 USAC Midget titles 111 USAC Midget wins (record) Mel Kenyon, USAC.

body: Rich Vogler won five USAC National Midget championships and the 1980 and 1989 USAC Sprint Car titles. His 95 National Midget wins rank second all-time, and he won the inaugural 1987 Chili Bowl and the Hut Hundred eight times. "Rapid Rich" Vogler of Glen Ellyn, Illinois, the son of midget winner Don Vogler, was the most prolific winner of USAC's short-track era. In 1980 he became the first driver to win the USAC Sprint and Midget championships in the same year. He won five National Midget titles, in 1978, 1980, 1983, 1986 and 1988, and Sprint titles in 1980 and 1989. His 134 USAC national wins break down to 95 Midget, 35 Sprint and four Silver Crown. Only A.J. Foyt has more. Vogler won the Hut Hundred eight times and the 4-Crown midget race four times. He also won the inaugural Chili Bowl in 1987, and his 16 wins in 100-lap midget races are the most of anyone. He made five Indianapolis 500 starts, with a best of eighth in 1989. Vogler was killed on July 21, 1990, while leading a sprint car race at Salem Speedway, five days before his 40th birthday. He was runner-up in the national standings three years in a row before winning the 1963 USAC National Midget championship. body: Pancho Carter was USAC's first career Triple Crown champion. He won the 1972 National Midget title, the 1974 and 1976 Sprint Car titles and the 1978 Silver Crown title. He also made 17 Indianapolis 500 starts, won the 1985 Indy pole and won the 1981 Michigan 500. Pancho Carter set the template for USAC versatility. The son of USAC Hall of Famer Duane Carter, he became the organization's first career Triple Crown champion and showed a generation of short-track drivers that one racer could master midgets, sprints and Silver Crown cars. He won the 1972 USAC National Midget title and Sprint Car titles in 1974 and 1976. In 1978 he won the Silver Crown title, then called the USAC National Dirt Championship. He scored 70 USAC national feature wins across those series. Carter was the 1974 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year and made 17 Indy 500 starts. He won the pole in 1985 and finished third in 1982. He also won the 1981 Michigan 500. He is a member of both the National Sprint Car and National Midget Halls of Fame and the USAC Hall of Fame. body: Tony Stewart is the first driver to win all three USAC national championships in one season, sweeping the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown titles in 1995. He won the 1997 IndyCar title and three NASCAR Cup championships (2002, 2005 and 2011). As a car owner he has nine World of Outlaws titles with Danny Lasoski and Donny Schatz, the 2026 High Limit title with Rico Abreu, seven USAC Sprint and seven Silver Crown owner championships, two NASCAR Cup and two Xfinity owner titles, and the 2023 NHRA Funny Car title. The Columbus, Indiana, driver won the 1994 USAC National Midget title. In 1995 he won the Midget, Sprint and Silver Crown championships, the first driver ever to sweep all three in a single season. He won 27 USAC National Midget races, 10 Sprint races and three Silver Crown races. Stewart won the 1997 Indy Racing League title and started on the pole for the 1996 Indianapolis 500. He then won three NASCAR Cup championships as a driver, in 2002, 2005 and 2011, the last as an owner-driver for Stewart-Haas Racing. He is the only driver to win championships in both IndyCar and NASCAR. He also won the Brickyard 400 in 2005 and 2007, the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals in 2002 and 2007, and the 2006 IROC championship. As a car owner, his record is separate from those driving titles. Tony Stewart Racing won nine World of Outlaws Sprint Car owner championships: the first with Danny Lasoski in 2001, in the team's inaugural season after Stewart formed TSR in November 2000, and eight more with Donny Schatz in 2008, 2009, 2012 and 2014 through 2018. Schatz joined TSR for the 2008 season after winning the 2006 and 2007 Outlaws titles with his own Donny Schatz Motorsports team. He and TSR parted ways on August 12, 2025, during a winless season; Kerry Madsen finished 2025 in the No. 15. TSR has not won another World of Outlaws title since Schatz's last one in 2018 (Brad Sweet won the series in 2020 and 2022). In 2026, after that split, Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing won the High Limit Racing owner title with Rico Abreu, Abreu's second straight High Limit driving championship and Stewart's first as a High Limit owner; Abreu's 2025 High Limit title was with his own team. Official USAC entrant-champion records credit Stewart with seven National Sprint Car owner titles and seven Silver Crown owner titles. The Sprint titles were with J.J. Yeley (2003), Josh Wise (2006) and Levi Jones (2007, 2009, 2010 and 2011), and Bryan Clauson (2013). The Silver Crown titles were with Yeley (2002 and 2003) and Dave Steele (2004 and 2005) under East-Stewart Racing, co-owned with Bob East, then with Jones (2010 and 2011) and Bobby East (2013) under Tony Stewart Racing / Tony Stewart/Curb-Agajanian Racing. Two often-cited years are not official Stewart owner titles: Jay Drake won the 2004 Sprint driver championship in a TSR car, but the USAC Sprint entrant title that year went to Dynamics, Inc. #69; Bobby East won the 2012 Silver Crown driver championship in a TSR car, but the official entrant title that year went to RW Motorsports/Curb-Agajanian Racing #17. Stewart-Haas Racing added NASCAR Cup owner championships in 2011, with Stewart driving, and in 2014 with Kevin Harvick. SHR also won two NASCAR Xfinity Series owner championships with Cole Custer in the No. 00: the 2018 owners title (Custer finished second in driver points to Tyler Reddick) and the 2023 title, when Custer also won the driver championship. SHR did not win a NASCAR Truck Series owner championship. In 2023 Matt Hagan won the NHRA Funny Car world championship for Tony Stewart Racing, the team's first NHRA title. In 2024 Stewart drove the team's Top Fuel dragster himself, reached two final rounds, made the Countdown to the Championship and was named NHRA Rookie of the Year. He was inducted into the National Midget Hall of Fame in 2001, the USAC Hall of Fame in 2016, the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2019, the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2020 and the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2022. title: Dave Darland “The People's Champ”
text: USAC Triple Crown. Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins.…
body: Dave Darland, the "People's Champ," is a USAC Triple Crown champion with titles in Silver Crown (1997), Sprint (1999) and Midget (2001–02). He retired in 2023 with 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins, then the record, and a record 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins. Dave Darland was USAC's everyman champion. Fans called him the "People's Champ." Over nearly four decades he made more USAC national starts than anyone, 1,334, and he showed that a local Indiana sprint car racer could become one of the sport's all-time greats. Born in 1966 in Lincoln, Indiana, he won four national titles: Silver Crown in 1997, Sprint in 1999, and Midget in 2001 and 2002. That made him the third career Triple Crown champion. His 62 USAC National Sprint Car wins were the record when he retired in 2023. His 20 Indiana Sprint Week wins are still the most of any driver. He won 115 USAC features nationally and regionally, including 30 National Midget and 14 Silver Crown wins. He won at least one USAC national feature in a record 24 straight seasons, 1993 through 2016. Along the way he won Turkey Night, the midget classic, twice. Darland is a member of the USAC Hall of Fame. body: J.J. Yeley swept all three USAC national championships in 2003, joining Tony Stewart as the only single-season Triple Crown winners. His 24 USAC wins that year broke A.J. Foyt's single-season record, and he also won the 2001 Sprint and 2002 Silver Crown titles. J.J. Yeley's 2003 season remains the high-water mark for a USAC driver. Racing Tony Stewart's sprint and Silver Crown cars and the Steve Lewis midget Stewart had driven in 1995, he won all three national championships and 24 USAC races. That broke the single-season record of 19 set by A.J. Foyt. Yeley won Indiana Sprint Week and USAC Sprint Rookie of the Year in 1997. He finished ninth in the 1998 Indianapolis 500 despite a first-lap spin. After an IndyCar run in 2000, he returned to USAC. He won the Sprint title in 2001, the Silver Crown title in 2002, and then the 2003 sweep, joining Stewart as the only drivers to win the Triple Crown in a single season. body: Tracy Hines is a USAC Triple Crown champion with Silver Crown (2000), Sprint (2002) and Midget (2015) titles. He won 91 USAC national races, including 47 in sprint cars, and he won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons. Tracy Hines spent most of a quarter-century as a full-time competitor in all three USAC national divisions. He was the son of a New Castle, Indiana, midget racing family, and his father Jim and brother Ted were champions too. He later helped build other drivers' programs as a team executive. He broke through in 1996, winning his first National Midget race at Winchester in his first start back from a fiery crash. Hines won the Silver Crown title in 2000 and the Sprint title in 2002. In 2015, after announcing his retirement midseason, he won the Midget title and completed the Triple Crown. He scored 91 USAC national wins, including 47 in sprint cars, 35 in midgets and nine in Silver Crown. He won at least one national feature in 19 straight seasons, 1996 through 2014. body: Kenny Weld was the first four-time Knoxville Nationals winner and the man to beat in Pennsylvania in the early 1970s. He later made his mark as a builder. Kenny Weld grew up in a Kansas City racing family. At 18 he won the 1964 Knoxville Nationals, and he won again in 1965, 1972 and 1973 to become the event's first four-time winner. Driving the Weikert Livestock Special in Pennsylvania, he won 43 features in 1973 and a record fifth straight Williams Grove track title in 1974. Discovered in California in 1968, he raced anywhere that paid, which kept him from piling up records with any one sanctioning body. He won the 1971 Knoxville Nationals and the Western World Championship that same season, then won 44 features in 1972. In 1976 he won the Hulman Classic at Terre Haute. He also co-designed the Maxwell sprint car and made two Indianapolis 500 starts. With long hair and a charisma few others had, he was one of the most beloved drivers in the sport and a big draw everywhere he raced. Crashes in 1976 and 1981 cut his career short. title: Jac Haudenschild “The Wild Child”
text: Old School Legends. Jac Haudenschild, "The Wild Child," was the most fearless driver in World of Outlaws history. He won 72 series features and three Kings Royals, and fans never took their eyes off him. Pronounced HOWD-en-shield, Jac Haudenschild's last name tripped up…
body: Jac Haudenschild, "The Wild Child," was the most fearless driver in World of Outlaws history. He won 72 series features and three Kings Royals, and fans never took their eyes off him. Pronounced HOWD-en-shield, Jac Haudenschild's last name tripped up announcers for years, and the mispronunciations gave way to the nickname "The Wild Child," one that fit his fearless driving style perfectly. The Wooster, Ohio, driver was the most daring the World of Outlaws ever saw, and his signature run around the outer edge of the speedway became known as the Haud Line. Even from ninth or 10th he could amaze a crowd, and he never burned a bridge, driving for 14 different winning car owners in the series. He won 72 World of Outlaws features, from the 1982 Eldora Nationals to his last series win at Eldora in 2010. His best points finish was second in 1995. He won the Kings Royal three times (1987, 1994, 1998), the Gold Cup three times and the 2003 Mopar Million. He was inducted into the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 2009 while still racing, and ran his final race at the 2021 World Finals. His son, Sheldon Haudenschild, has continued that exciting legacy, thrilling a new generation of fans on the Haud Line, a line that was clearly in his DNA. 72 World of Outlaws wins Kings Royal: 1987, 1994, 1998 National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (2009) 72 WoO wins Crown jewel: 3 Kings Royals Jac Haudenschild with his son Sheldon Haudenschild (cropped to Jac), World of Outlaws.

title: Bobby Allen “Scruffy”
text: Old School Legends. Bobby Allen did a lot with a little. In 1990 the low-budget racer drove his homebuilt No. 1a past Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals, still remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. Bobby Allen grew up in Miami racing go-karts, then…
body: Bobby Allen did a lot with a little. In 1990 the low-budget racer drove his homebuilt No. 1a past Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals, still remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. Bobby Allen grew up in Miami racing go-karts, then headed to Pennsylvania as a teenager because that was where the sprint cars ran three and four nights a week. He became one of the sport's original outlaws. He was known for doing a lot with a little. He built his own chassis, put together his own engines and made his own setup calls on the familiar No. 1a, spending what money he had on the car rather than on how it looked. On Aug. 18, 1990, in front of about 18,000 fans, his homebuilt car beat the well-funded Sammy Swindell to win the Knoxville Nationals. It is remembered as the biggest upset in the event's history. He won more than 275 sprint car features, including 30 with the World of Outlaws and 46 with the All Star Circuit of Champions, where he won the 1980 title. He entered the National Sprint Car Hall of Fame in 1988. He later owned Shark Racing of Hanover, Pa., and in 2014 took the team on the World of Outlaws tour full time with his grandson, Logan Schuchart, and his son, Jacob Allen. Jacob drove the team's No. 1A until he stepped away from full-time driving in April 2025. After a three-race stint by Cale Thomas, Ashton Torgerson took over the seat later that month, and Jacob stayed on to run the No. 1A as crew chief. Bobby Allen died Oct. 5, 2025, at 81. 1990 Knoxville Nationals winner 30 World of Outlaws wins 1980 All Star Circuit of Champions champion National Sprint Car Hall of Fame (1988) 30 WoO wins Crown jewel: 1990 Knoxville Nationals Bobby Allen at Hagerstown, May 24, 1987, World of Outlaws.

body: Brad Doty was a World of Outlaws winner and 1987 points runner-up whose driving career ended in the 1988 Kings Royal. He stayed in the sport as a promoter and its best-known TV analyst, and fans have never stopped loving him for it. Brad Doty of Ohio was World of Outlaws and Knoxville Nationals Rookie of the Year in 1982. He won 18 World of Outlaws features and 73 sprint car features in all, and he finished second to Steve Kinser in the 1987 World of Outlaws standings. A crash on the opening lap of the 1988 Kings Royal at Eldora left him paralyzed from the chest down. He never left the sport. He started the Brad Doty Classic in 1989 and from 1992 became the best-known television voice of winged sprint car racing.
